text:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty incident INC-78124 triggered for service 'prod-billing' — High error rate (5xx) observed. Link: https://pagerduty.com/INCIDENTS/INC-78124

incident-bot: Automatic page sent to rotation 'billing-oncall' (escalation policy: billing-prod-policy).

alice (SRE): wait, I'm seeing traces for prod-search, not billing.

ben (oncall): acking INC-78124 now — I got the page.

carol (support): customers reporting search failures, multiple 503s across EU region. Just triaged two small clusters.

alice (SRE): ben — which service did PD show when you acked?

ben (oncall): the pager said 'prod-billing'. I assumed billing team would know, started to look.

alice (SRE): that's the problem — the alert's routing rule flipped. The metric name is search.latency.p95, check tags.

ben (oncall): oh crap. I don't own search. @dave can you take? I'm going to escalate.

incident-bot: INC-78124 escalated to dave (eng) after 5m of no owner transfer.

dave (eng): pulling logs. I see the ingestion path failing for search indexer in eu-west-1. Example log:```ERROR 2026-03-15T09:12:02Z service=prod-search component=indexer msg="shard write failed" err=EIO
trace_id=tx-9a7f5```

alice (SRE): PD payload for alert shows:```metric: search.latency.p95
service: prod-search
tags: region=eu-west-1,env=prod``` but the PagerDuty rule matched to prod-billing service via an older tag mapping.

eve (infra): we're seeing a config deploy to alert-router 03:11 UTC that updated tag->service mappings. Recent commit: `router: map: billing: owner=payments` — looks like a YAML indentation bug merged.

carol (support): customer impact: 14 accounts in EU experiencing search failures, 3 support tickets open, two customers on Slack complaining.

ben (oncall): I started a temporary suppression on prod-billing to stop noisy pages, but that prevented correct owners from getting notified. sorry.

alice (SRE): suppression on billing was applied to the PD service level — that blocked search owners because the router forwarded to billing. don’t suppress at service-level in this window.

dave (eng): mitigation plan: 1) re-route active incident to correct on-call (prod-search-oncall). 2) roll back alert-router config to last-good. 3) scale indexer pool + restart affected shards. 4) postmortem + corrective action on deploy gating.

alice (SRE): commands:```# re-route in pagerduty (admin)
pdctl reroute INC-78124 --to-service prod-search --note "misroute fix"```

alice (SRE): I'm running that now.

incident-bot: pdctl executed by alice (SRE): reroute INC-78124 -> prod-search. New notifications dispatched to rotation 'search-oncall'.

pagerbot: Notification: INC-78124 reassigned to prod-search-oncall, paging dave (eng) and foward rotation.

ben (oncall): thanks. I removed the suppression on prod-billing.

dave (eng): scaled indexer pool x2 and restarted replicas in eu-west-1 — seeing reduced 5xxs.

carol (support): confirmed with customers: search responses are back to normal for the impacted accounts. I'll update tickets and send short incident notice.

eve (infra): rolling back alert-router to commit 7a2f9b (pre-incident). Patch queued to add unit test for tag mapping.

alice (SRE): root cause: bad alert-router config change (YAML mapping bug) + mistaken service-level suppression by oncall. Contributing factor: PD routing rules assume tag mapping correctness.

ben (oncall): huge apologies — suppression is my fault. Will follow the runbook for suppression scope (only endpoint-level next time). :grimacing:

dave (eng): incident status: mitigated at 09:32 UTC. will keep monitoring for 30m.

incident-bot: INC-78124 status changed to 'acknowledged' -> 'resolved' by dave (eng). Resolution note: re-route + indexer scale + rollback alert-router.

carol (support): Customer impact summary for postmortem: 14 accounts affected, 0 data loss, ~20 minutes degradation, EU-only, root cause: routing misconfiguration.

alice (SRE): follow-ups: 1) add CI test for alert-router tag->service mapping, 2) update oncall runbook about suppression scope, 3) PD rule audit to ensure service names are explicit not implicit mapping, 4) Postmortem doc and action owners.

dave (eng): assigning followups: alert-router CI test -> eve (infra); oncall runbook update -> ben (oncall); PD audit -> alice (SRE); postmortem write-up -> carol (support).

ben (oncall): will write a short note to rotation to apologize and summarize.

alice (SRE): thanks everyone. closing thread once postmortem link is up. :white_check_mark:
